stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = 4 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 5 \) for \( 0 \le t \le 5 \). At time t = 0 the particle is at \( \theta = 0 \), and its angle increases at the constant rate \( \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{10} \). Using a calculator, find the time t at which the x-coordinate of the particle's position is 7. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The angle starts at 0 and grows at a constant rate, so \( \theta(t) = \frac{\pi t}{10} \). The coordinate is \( x = r\cos\theta = \left(4 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 5\right) \cos{\left(\theta \right)} \), so in terms of time \( x(t) = \left(4 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{10} \right)} + 5\right) \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{10} \right)} \).
Solve \( \left(4 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{10} \right)} + 5\right) \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{10} \right)} = 7 \) on \( 0 \le t \le 5 \) with a calculator. The only solution is \( t \approx 1.837 \).

options.derivation: the angle rounded to one decimal place before it was converted to a time
the equation solved in theta and the angle reported in place of the time
r treated as the x-coordinate, so the time at which r equals the value is reported
